data.name: Metal as Phuk
data.detailed_description:
ABOUT THIS GAME:


Sold in over 90+ countries around the world and praised as one of the funniest and most clever RPG's of all time, Metal as Phuk is a Mature, Turn-Based, Crude Comedy that has one goal and one goal only: To Make You Laugh!
Play as Chael, the only surviving Paladin of the Metal Order as he embarks on his journey to stop The Dark Bards before they can summon A'Marthius, a MONSTROUS Demon D-Bag who wants nothing more than to see the world burn! A dark, insidious world full of Epic Metal References awaits you as your party battles their way through Unholy Adversaries, Big Bad Bosses, and Smaller, but -STILL- Bad Bosses! Phuk, the God of Metal watches over you on your journey... but do you have what it takes to be Metal, as Phuk?



This game features:



  • Dozens of Sick-Ass Metal References!
  • Awesome Boss Battles!
  • Turn-Based Combat System with Epic Loot and Leveling!
  • Hilarious Items and Easter Eggs Hidden Throughout the World!
  • Four Kickass Party Members with Four Kickass Classes!
  • 4 Dozen Epic Songs to Headbang to until your BRAIN FALLS OUT OF YOUR $%^&ING SKULL!
    (Crankage Games is not responsible for Cranial Extraction due to excessive headbanging...)
  • Original Storyline! (Well, as original as one can get, I mean, C'mon, Right?!)
  • "Herbs"... !

... And a Phuk-Ton More!

data.short_description: Metal as Phuk is a Mature, Turn-Based, Crude Comedy RPG that has one goal and one goal only: To Make You Laugh! Play as Chael, the last Paladin of the Metal Order, as he embarks on his journey to stop The Dark Bards before they can summon A'Marthius, a MONSTROUS Demon D-Bag!

reviews.review:
Metal as Phuk is an indie role-playing game that proudly embraces outrageous humor, heavy metal culture, and retro RPG design with absolutely no intention of appealing to mainstream tastes. Developed and published by Crankage Games, it delivers an adventure that mixes classic turn-based combat with an abundance of crude jokes, absurd situations, and over-the-top characters. Rather than presenting a serious fantasy epic, the game thrives on parody and self-awareness, creating a world where every quest, conversation, and battle is infused with exaggerated personality. Players step into the role of Chael, the final surviving Paladin of the Metal Order, whose mission is to stop the sinister Dark Bards from unleashing the fearsome demon A'Marthius. While the central storyline follows a familiar save-the-world formula, it constantly twists expectations through ridiculous scenarios, making the narrative feel unpredictable and consistently entertaining.

The game's greatest strength lies in its commitment to its unique identity. Every location is packed with eccentric NPCs, bizarre monsters, hidden references, and humorous dialogue that rewards players who enjoy exploring every corner of the world. Heavy metal fans will immediately notice countless nods to the genre through character names, equipment, music, and jokes inspired by famous bands and albums. However, the writing extends beyond simple references by incorporating satire, fantasy clichés, and intentionally exaggerated storytelling that gives the adventure its own distinct personality. The dialogue rarely slows down, constantly delivering jokes and surprising interactions that prevent the experience from becoming repetitive. Although the humor is intentionally juvenile and outrageous, it remains surprisingly creative, ensuring that even routine quests are filled with memorable moments.

Gameplay follows the foundations of traditional turn-based RPGs, making it approachable for players familiar with classic role-playing adventures. Battles revolve around assembling a party of four unique classes, leveling up characters, learning stronger abilities, collecting better equipment, and overcoming increasingly dangerous enemies. Combat mechanics are straightforward without becoming dull, allowing progression to feel rewarding throughout the campaign. Exploration is equally important, as hidden treasures, optional encounters, secret references, and collectible items encourage players to stray from the main path. Boss encounters stand out in particular, combining humorous presentation with more demanding combat that requires players to make effective use of their growing arsenal of skills and equipment. While the mechanics do not reinvent the genre, they remain polished enough to support the game's stronger emphasis on entertainment and comedy.

Visually, Metal as Phuk embraces a nostalgic pixel-art presentation reminiscent of classic RPG Maker titles while maintaining its own colorful identity. Character sprites, environments, and enemy designs all reinforce the game's exaggerated tone, allowing its comedic style to shine throughout the adventure. The soundtrack is another highlight, featuring energetic compositions inspired by heavy metal that complement both exploration and combat. The music consistently reinforces the atmosphere and helps distinguish the game from many other indie RPGs that rely on more traditional fantasy soundtracks. Combined with expressive animations and humorous visual details scattered across the world, the presentation demonstrates genuine enthusiasm and passion from its creators despite the modest scale of the project.

The game is not without its drawbacks, and many of them stem directly from its creative choices. Its humor is intentionally offensive, featuring constant profanity, sexual jokes, crude language, alcohol references, drug-related humor, and other mature content that many players may find excessive. Rather than using occasional shock value, the game builds its entire identity around pushing boundaries, meaning those who dislike vulgar comedy are unlikely to enjoy the experience regardless of its solid gameplay. Some jokes inevitably land better than others, and the relentless pace of comedic dialogue may occasionally overshadow character development or emotional storytelling. Players seeking a more serious fantasy RPG with complex themes and dramatic narrative moments may find the experience lacking in depth.

Despite these limitations, Metal as Phuk succeeds because it never compromises its vision. It confidently delivers exactly what it promises: an unapologetically ridiculous adventure filled with heavy metal inspiration, entertaining turn-based combat, memorable boss battles, rewarding exploration, and an endless stream of outrageous comedy. Its willingness to fully commit to such a specific style helps it stand apart from countless indie RPGs that play things more safely. While its crude humor will naturally divide audiences, those who appreciate irreverent comedy and classic role-playing mechanics will likely discover an experience bursting with personality, creativity, and enthusiasm. It may not become a universal favorite, but within its niche, it successfully offers a distinctive and highly memorable adventure.

Rating: 8/10
